evidence.reference_title: Molecular characterization of a case of atransferrinemia.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary atransferrinemia is a rare but instructive disorder that has previously been reported in only 8 patients in 6 families. It is characterized by microcytic anemia and by iron loading, and can be treated effectively by plasma infusions. We now report the first case known in the United States. We determined the sequences flanking the exons of the human transferrin gene and sequenced all of the exons and some of the flanking regions of the patient's DNA and that of her parents. The patient's DNA revealed a 10-base pair (bp) deletion, followed by a 9-bp insertion of a duplicated sequence. There was also a G-->C transversion at complementary DNA (cDNA) nt 1429, predicting that a proline was substituted for the alanine in amino acid position 477 (Ala 477 Pro). The latter mutation occurs at an evolutionarily highly conserved site; 704 control alleles were screened and this point mutation was not found. Each of the patient's transferrin genes contains one mutation, ie, the patient is a compound heterozygote for these mutations, because one was found in each of her parents. In addition to these mutations, which we regard to be causative in the patient's atransferrinemia, a silent polymorphism at cDNA 1572 G-->C was found in exon 13 as well as 2 previously unreported polymorphisms at IVS8 + 62 c-->t and IVS14-4 c-->a. The mutation in nt 1572 and that in intron 8 were common in the general population; the intron 14 mutation is rare.

evidence.reference_title: Revisiting Congenital Atransferrinemia: A Rare but Treatable Cause of Pediatric Heart Failure.
evidence.snippet: A 13-year-old girl born of second-degree consanguinity presented with heart failure, severe anemia, and diabetes mellitus. Her clinical course included heart failure at six months, diabetes at age seven, and progressive LV systolic dysfunction. Iron studies revealed low TIBC, elevated ferritin, low transferrin saturation, and undetectable transferrin levels (<75 mg/dL). Echocardiography showed severe biventricular systolic dysfunction. There was an incidentally detected 4 mm PDA (Fig. 4). As the age advanced, heart failure worsened disproportionately. Cardiac MRI confirmed myocardial iron overload, and genetic testing identified a novel mutation, confirming the diagnosis. This highlights the importance of early recognition and genetic analysis in hereditary atransferrinemia.

evidence.snippet: DNA analysis of the serum transferrin gene in the patient revealed a previously undescribed mutation in exon 4, a G-->A transition at cDNA 410(Cys137Tyr).

evidence.reference_title: Hypotransferrinemia leading to fatal hemochromatosis without anemia.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed homozygous TF variant NM_001063.3:c.1108G>A , p.(Glu370Lys). No other variants were found in the gene panel.

evidence.reference_title: Revisiting Congenital Atransferrinemia: A Rare but Treatable Cause of Pediatric Heart Failure.
evidence.snippet: Targeted exome sequencing in the proband revealed a novel splice site variant, NC_000003.12:g.133778575_133778576del(NM_001063.3:c.2063-11_2063-10del) in intron 16 of TF in the homozygous state. Segregation analysis in the mother confirmed the variant to be present in the heterozygous state. This variant was not observed in population databases and in-house whole-exome sequencing (WES) data of 1246 individuals of Indian origin (Fig 7). This variant has been classified as a variant of uncertain significance according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary hypotransferrinemia can lead to elevated transferrin saturation and, when associated to HFE or HAMP mutations, to iron overload.
evidence.snippet: We show that, besides increasing serum transferrin saturation without iron overload, hypotransferrinemia, when associated to mutations in HFE or HAMP or to acquired factors, can lead to clinically relevant iron burden.

nodes.description: A homozygous intronic variant in a 13-year-old with anemia, cardiac/hepatic iron and diabetes. The source explicitly classifies it as a variant of uncertain significance; rarity and segregation do not establish a splice defect.

The first molecularly characterized US case had two different alleles: p.Ala477Pro and a 10-bp deletion with 9-bp insertion. Segregation and conservation supported causality; the accessible abstract does not report a secretion assay.

Homozygous c.1108G>A in two adult sisters with severe hypotransferrinemia and iron overload; classified as likely pathogenic by the 2025 authors using prediction and segregation, without a reported functional assay.
Reported with severe anemia; it is not specific to myocardial iron injury.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital Hypotransferrinemia, an Unusual Cause of Iron Deficiency Anemia: Report of Two Cases.
evidence.snippet: Manifestations of severe anemia develop in infancy or early childhood, i.e. pallor, fatigue, anorexia, irritability, tachycardia, systolic murmur, hepatomegaly, growth retardation and recurrent infections.

nodes.description: Blood removal can lower iron burden when erythropoiesis and hemoglobin permit. The guideline advises adjustment to hemoglobin, ferritin and symptoms. One nonanemic adult sister tolerated monthly phlebotomy without transferrin replacement; this must not be generalized to severely anemic children.

evidence.reference_title: Behandeling atransferrinemie (anemie) - Richtlijn - Richtlijnendatabase
evidence.snippet: In geval van ijzerstapeling, adviseert de werkgroep aderlatingen op geleide van Hb, ferritine en klachten. Als alternatief kan chelatie therapie worden gegeven.

evidence.reference_title: Hypotransferrinemia leading to fatal hemochromatosis without anemia.
evidence.snippet: Bloodletting (300cc month ly w ithout plasma or purified transferrin supplementation) was well tolerated and efficient ; after one year of treatment, the ferritin level was 115µg/L without anemia.

evidence.reference_title: https://richtlijnendatabase.nl/gerelateerde_documenten/file/5656/1/Donker%20Guidelines%20anemia%20Blood%202014.pdf
evidence.snippet: In case of systemic iron loading, phlebotomies are recommended. If phlebotomies are not tolerated because of decreasing Hb, chelation therapy is rec ommended.

nodes.description: The spontaneous splice-donor allele produces severe transferrin deficiency, anemia and nonhematopoietic iron loading. The 2011 study compared replacement, washed wild-type red-cell transfusion and myeloablation followed by transferrin. Replacement improved hematologic and hepcidin readouts; withdrawal allowed recurrence. Suppression of erythropoiesis and restoration of transferrin make separable contributions. The study does not establish apoptosis of immature erythrocytes, a complete human signaling chain or universal clinical rescue.

nodes.description: Two recessive gavi splice alleles predict truncated transferrin-a and produce hypochromic anemia with early lethality. Morpholino knockdown reproduced reduced hemoglobin and tissue-iron staining; transferrin-a cRNA partially restored them. TfR2 knockdown reduced hepcidin without anemia, whereas anemia induced outside the transferrin pathway did not lower basal embryonic hepcidin. The complete main body, methods and captions were reviewed; separate supplementary objects were not assessed.
